title: Enrolling in television school
summary: Hall studied television direction at a school on 57th Street in 1950.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now, when did you go into the TV school?
Uh-huh. Where was this? In New York, naturally, but --
SRT, it was on 57th Street. [School of Radio Techniques]

And I was looking through a Sunday Times Magazine Section, and Jackie Robinson had just became a news person on NBC, and I saw this ad for TV, TV school, and I thought, well, you know, if he's in front of the mike, maybe

I could be behind the mike, you know, And so I went over and took the course and -- as class producer, had all the qualifications of becoming a director, which was my ambition. But I would have settled for anything then except a grip.

So I was working at the Blue Angel at the time, and I was going to school during the day. And I'd meet all the personalities that came in, including Yul Brynner, and we were talking about Mike Levine. And he used to come in, all the TV guys, people, you know, and a lot of directors.

So I was invited in a clients' booth to all the major shows like Montgomery Presents and Studio One and the Perry Como show I used to catch every day coming home from school, because I knew the musical contractor, and I could sit in and listen to the directions.
And I was very interested in that part of television. And what whetted my appetite was when I started with Hazel Scott in 1950 at the Dumont Show, and I used to go in and watch the screen, you know.
So I gave myself five years to get employed, but it didn't happen.
